result.summary: The image shows a wide, multi-lane one-way urban street with signalized pedestrian crossings and wide sidewalks. While the infrastructure is in good condition, the multi-lane configuration and lack of physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions increase pedestrian exposure.

hazards.name: Multi-lane one-way roadway
hazards.description: The three-lane one-way configuration can encourage higher vehicle speeds and increases the risk of multiple-threat crashes for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross three lanes of traffic without a refuge island or curb extensions to reduce exposure.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light, reducing conflicts with turning traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Replace the existing colored pavement with high-visibility continental-style markings to improve driver awareness of the crossing.

result.summary: The image depicts a dense urban environment with wide, well-maintained sidewalks and a textured brick crossing area. While the street design is pedestrian-oriented, the lack of high-visibility continental crosswalk markings and the presence of large planters near the curb may impact visibility and safety.

hazards.name: Low-contrast crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The brick-textured crossing lacks high-visibility white continental markings, which can reduce its visibility to drivers in low-light or wet conditions.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from street furniture
hazards.description: Large planters located near the curb edge may partially obstruct the sightlines between drivers and shorter pedestrians, such as children, waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground sidewalk near the curb

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Add white continental or ladder-style markings over or adjacent to the brick pavers to significantly increase the visibility of the crossing zone.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear information on the remaining crossing time.

result.summary: The environment features wide, well-maintained sidewalks in a high-density commercial area. However, the intersection lacks marked crosswalks and visible pedestrian signals, creating a gap in the pedestrian network despite the presence of traffic lights.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized urban intersection featuring a wide, brick-textured crosswalk and standard pedestrian signals. While basic infrastructure is present, the significant crossing distance and potential sightline obstructions from corner scaffolding and parked vehicles increase pedestrian exposure.

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway increases the time pedestrians are exposed to potential vehicle conflicts.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground crosswalk across the main street.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Scaffolding on the corner and parked vehicles near the intersection may block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Far left corner and along the curbs.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility of pedestrians waiting to cross.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles receive a green light.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve sightlines for both drivers and pedestrians.
